voiceover: When AI writes code, it isn't looking anything up. It's predicting. A language model breaks text into tokens: chunks of characters, often pieces of words. Then it guesses the most likely next token, adds it, and guesses again. One token at a time. It learned those patterns from a huge amount of text and code during training. That's why it's great at common patterns, like a for loop or a login form, and why it can sound confident about stuff that's wrong. It's predicting what looks right, not checking what is right. Part two: why it forgets what you told it earlier.
